approved_input.value: Visual Outcomes and Patient-Reported Symptoms after Bilateral Implantation of an Extended Depth of Focus or a Full Range of Vision Intraocular Lens

The TECNIS PureSee is a non-diffractive extended depth of focus (EDOF) intraocular lens. Its design may reduce dysphotopsias and improve contrast sensitivity compared with diffractive lenses. A randomized controlled trial suggested better intermediate and near vision than a monofocal control, with similar contrast sensitivity, distance vision, and dysphotopsia profiles.1

The TECNIS Odyssey is a full range of vision intraocular lens. Current reports suggest high visual acuity and spectacle independence at distance, intermediate, and near.2,3

These reports concern the individual lens technologies. They do not establish which lens will provide better outcomes in the population proposed here. We would like to characterize vision and patient-reported symptoms in two cohorts followed using the same assessment schedule.

The objective is to describe and compare binocular visual outcomes, spectacle use, satisfaction, and visual disturbances after bilateral PureSee or bilateral Odyssey implantation through 6 months after second-eye surgery.

Lens selection will already have been made by the treating surgeon and patient as part of routine care before study enrollment. Enrollment will not determine lens selection. There will be no randomization, no masking, and no change to the planned clinical treatment. Each subject will receive the same lens model in both eyes. This study does not involve mix-and-match implantation.

1. Corbett D, Black D, Roberts TV, Cronin B, Gunn D, Bala C, Versace P, Tsai L, Papadatou E, Alarcon A, Vilupuru S. Quality of vision clinical outcomes for a new fully-refractive extended depth of focus Intraocular Lens. Eye. 2024;38(S1):9-14. doi:10.1038/s41433-024-03039-8
2. Hacopian AG, Brunson PB, Hall B. Patient Reported Outcomes and Visual Acuity After Bilateral Implantation of a Next Generation Presbyopia Correcting Intraocular Lens. OPTH. 2026;20:1-8. doi:10.2147/OPTH.S572703
3. Bissen-Miyajima H, Midorikawa M, Fujisaki R, Ota Y, Minami K, Honda R. Early Clinical Results of a Newly Developed Continuous Range of Vision Intraocular Lens. Ophthalmol Ther. 2025;14(11):2937-2945. doi:10.1007/s40123-025-01235-7

The hypothesis is that bilateral implantation of PureSee or Odyssey intraocular lenses will be associated with good distance and intermediate visual outcomes and high patient satisfaction. Near vision, spectacle use, and reports of visual disturbances may differ between the two cohorts. This observational study is intended to describe those outcomes; it is not designed to establish superiority of either lens.

paragraphs.text: To join, you must be at least 50 years old and planning surgery for age-related cataracts in both eyes. Your routine-care plan must already be to receive either TECNIS PureSee in both eyes or TECNIS Odyssey in both eyes. You must be willing and able to attend the scheduled assessments and must not have participated in another study during the 60 days before screening.

You cannot join if your surgeon considers that moderate-to-severe eye disease would increase the risk of complicated cataract surgery or prevent reliable vision testing. Other reasons you cannot join include pseudoexfoliation syndrome with significant weakness of the fibers supporting the lens; separation of these supporting fibers, called zonular dehiscence; a previous eye injury that affects vision; or previous surgery on the cornea to correct vision. A plan to use different lens models in your two eyes also prevents participation.

At the preoperative screening visit, you will go through informed consent. The study team will collect demographic information and your medical history and confirm the lens already selected during routine care and your corresponding study group. At an operative visit for each eye, you will have cataract surgery and implantation of the planned lens model. These operations follow your routine-care treatment plan rather than a lens choice made by the study.

The follow-up vision tests measure how clearly you see with both eyes together in bright lighting. Testing without correction means testing without glasses or other corrective lenses. Distance-corrected testing uses correction for distance vision, including when you look at an intermediate or near target. These tests measure your vision for the research.

At Month 1 after second-eye surgery, your distance vision will be tested both without and with correction. Your intermediate vision will also be tested without correction at 66 cm. The team will review medical problems and problems with the implanted lenses.

At Month 3, you will repeat the distance tests with and without correction and the intermediate test without correction at 66 cm. Near vision will be tested at 40 cm both without correction and with distance correction. You will complete the Assessment of IntraOcular Lens Implant Symptoms questionnaire, called AIOLIS. Medical problems and lens problems will also be reviewed.

At Month 6, the tests include distance vision with and without correction, intermediate vision at 66 cm without correction and with distance correction, and near vision at 40 cm without correction and with distance correction. A distance-corrected defocus curve will measure vision across a range of focus. You will complete the AIOLIS questionnaire again. The team will review medical problems and lens problems and complete the exit form.

Information about adverse events, meaning medical problems, and device deficiencies, meaning problems with the lenses, will be collected from consent through the final study contact. The scheduled reviews do not limit when an event may be reported.

approved_input.value: Visual Outcomes and Patient-Reported Symptoms after Bilateral Implantation of an Extended Depth of Focus or a Full Range of Vision Intraocular Lens

The TECNIS PureSee is a non-diffractive extended depth of focus (EDOF) intraocular lens. Its design may reduce dysphotopsias and improve contrast sensitivity compared with diffractive lenses. A randomized controlled trial suggested better intermediate and near vision than a monofocal control, with similar contrast sensitivity, distance vision, and dysphotopsia profiles.1

The TECNIS Odyssey is a full range of vision intraocular lens. Current reports suggest high visual acuity and spectacle independence at distance, intermediate, and near.2,3

These reports concern the individual lens technologies. They do not establish which lens will provide better outcomes in the population proposed here. We would like to characterize vision and patient-reported symptoms in two cohorts followed using the same assessment schedule.

The objective is to describe and compare binocular visual outcomes, spectacle use, satisfaction, and visual disturbances after bilateral PureSee or bilateral Odyssey implantation through 6 months after second-eye surgery.

Lens selection will already have been made by the treating surgeon and patient as part of routine care before study enrollment. Enrollment will not determine lens selection. There will be no randomization, no masking, and no change to the planned clinical treatment. Each subject will receive the same lens model in both eyes. This study does not involve mix-and-match implantation.

paragraphs.text: To take part, you must be at least 50 years old and undergoing surgery for age-related cataracts in both eyes. You and your treating surgeon must already have selected either TECNIS PureSee lenses for both eyes or TECNIS Odyssey lenses for both eyes during routine clinical care before enrollment. You must be willing and able to attend the scheduled study assessments and must not have participated in another study during the 60 days before screening.

You cannot take part if your surgeon determines that you have moderate-to-severe eye disease that increases the risk of complicated cataract surgery or prevents reliable vision testing. You also cannot take part if you have pseudoexfoliation syndrome with clinically significant weakness of the fibers that hold the lens in place, separation of those fibers (zonular dehiscence), a previous eye injury affecting vision, or previous surgery on the cornea to correct your vision. Planning to have different lens models implanted in your two eyes also makes you ineligible.

At the preoperative screening visit, you will be asked to give informed consent. The study team will collect basic information about you, called demographics, and your medical history. They will confirm your routine-care lens selection and the study group that matches it.

There will be an operative visit for each eye, when cataract surgery and implantation of the planned lens model will take place as part of your routine care. Joining the study does not select a different lens for you. The time between your two surgeries will follow routine clinical care; the study does not set a fixed interval.

The postoperative study assessments measure your vision rather than provide treatment. Vision tests will use both eyes together, called binocular testing. Tests described as photopic are done in bright lighting. Uncorrected tests measure your vision without glasses or other vision correction. Corrected distance tests use correction for distance vision; distance-corrected intermediate and near tests also use correction for distance vision. Every postoperative time point below is measured from surgery on your second eye.

At the Month 1 visit, 1 month after second-eye surgery, you will have binocular uncorrected and corrected photopic distance visual-acuity tests, which measure how clearly you see far away. You will also have binocular uncorrected photopic intermediate visual-acuity testing at 66 cm. The study team will monitor for adverse events, meaning health problems, and device deficiencies, meaning problems with the implanted lenses.

At the Month 3 visit, 3 months after second-eye surgery, you will again have binocular uncorrected and corrected photopic distance visual-acuity tests and binocular uncorrected photopic intermediate visual-acuity testing at 66 cm. You will also have binocular uncorrected and distance-corrected photopic near visual-acuity testing at 40 cm. You will complete the Assessment of IntraOcular Lens Implant Symptoms (AIOLIS) questionnaire about your symptoms. The study team will monitor for adverse events and device deficiencies.

At the Month 6 exit visit, 6 months after second-eye surgery, you will have binocular uncorrected and corrected photopic distance visual-acuity tests; binocular uncorrected and distance-corrected photopic intermediate visual-acuity tests at 66 cm; and binocular uncorrected and distance-corrected photopic near visual-acuity tests at 40 cm. A distance-corrected defocus curve will measure your vision across different focusing conditions while you use correction for distance vision. You will complete the AIOLIS questionnaire again. The study team will monitor for adverse events and device deficiencies and complete the exit form.

Information about adverse events and device deficiencies will be collected from the time you give consent through your final study contact. The scheduled reviews at Months 1, 3, and 6 are not the only times these problems may be reported.

approved_input.value: Visual Outcomes and Patient-Reported Symptoms after Bilateral Implantation of an Extended Depth of Focus or a Full Range of Vision Intraocular Lens

The TECNIS PureSee is a non-diffractive extended depth of focus (EDOF) intraocular lens. Its design may reduce dysphotopsias and improve contrast sensitivity compared with diffractive lenses. A randomized controlled trial suggested better intermediate and near vision than a monofocal control, with similar contrast sensitivity, distance vision, and dysphotopsia profiles.1

The TECNIS Odyssey is a full range of vision intraocular lens. Current reports suggest high visual acuity and spectacle independence at distance, intermediate, and near.2,3

These reports concern the individual lens technologies. They do not establish which lens will provide better outcomes in the population proposed here. We would like to characterize vision and patient-reported symptoms in two cohorts followed using the same assessment schedule.

The objective is to describe and compare binocular visual outcomes, spectacle use, satisfaction, and visual disturbances after bilateral PureSee or bilateral Odyssey implantation through 6 months after second-eye surgery.

Lens selection will already have been made by the treating surgeon and patient as part of routine care before study enrollment. Enrollment will not determine lens selection. There will be no randomization, no masking, and no change to the planned clinical treatment. Each subject will receive the same lens model in both eyes. This study does not involve mix-and-match implantation.

2. Hacopian AG, Brunson PB, Hall B. Patient Reported Outcomes and Visual Acuity After Bilateral Implantation of a Next Generation Presbyopia Correcting Intraocular Lens. OPTH. 2026;20:1-8. doi:10.2147/OPTH.S572703

Listed Fixed Clinical Boilerplate is authorized only where applicable and consistent with the approved source. The approved source supersedes boilerplate; boilerplate must not expand decision-making authority, termination grounds, completion criteria, procedures, or safety obligations.

When a section lists both Fixed Clinical Boilerplate and minimum evidence, include all material source facts and only applicable, nonconflicting boilerplate; omit boilerplate clauses that would alter a source rule.
Do not invent study-specific facts, procedures, risks, benefits, safety obligations, legal promises, or regulatory claims.
Return exactly one result for every requested section ID.
Use only the drafted or fixed_boilerplate outcome. Sparse sections may use only applicable, source-consistent listed Fixed Clinical Boilerplate.
Return structured section content, not a whole document or document markup.

Write separately contracted sections independently; do not repeat an exact sentence or paragraph, including any exact list item, across target sections unless the listed Fixed Clinical Boilerplate explicitly requires it. When contracts cover overlapping facts, express each section's distinct purpose without copying schedule prose verbatim.
Use participant-facing language for ICF sections.
For icf.key-information-summary, draft directly from its canonical summary obligations; keep each concept concise and never copy a complete detailed-section sentence or paragraph.

For a Sterling ICF, BACKGROUND owns lens descriptions, comparative evidence, the evidence gap, and rationale. PURPOSE must be concise and limited to the purpose, hypothesis, and primary endpoint; do not restate BACKGROUND.

ICF PROCEDURES owns detailed study activities and DURATION owns timing. Do not repeat their detail in PURPOSE, ALTERNATIVE TREATMENTS, VOLUNTARY PARTICIPATION/WITHDRAWAL, or the participant statement unless the Sterling Clause Contract explicitly requires it.

For Protocol sections, follow concept_ownership: explain owned concepts completely, keep brief_reference_only concepts concise, and do not re-explain do_not_restate concepts. Endpoint names, visit names and timing, identifiers, quantities, safety terms, and brief traceability cross-references may recur.

Protocol General Information is a compact synopsis; Objectives states the study purpose and objectives; Study Design owns the grouped endpoint inventory; Study Methods and Measurements owns what is measured, when, and how; Analysis Data Sets owns which observations enter populations or datasets; Statistical Methodology owns how endpoints are summarized or analyzed. Group shared-method endpoints and do not reproduce the endpoint inventory outside Study Design unless scientific meaning requires it.

Satisfy every section's content_expectations and cover every material value named by minimum_evidence, except that Section 15's source-derived table and notes carry its detailed inventory. Its adjacent prose should briefly introduce the table without restating its rows or notes.
Write clinical content that serves the section purpose. Omit self-referential filler, generic transitions, and repeated conclusions that add no source-supported information.

Use reference_detail_target_words only as a soft compression signal; semantic source coverage governs acceptance, and concise complete prose must not be padded, repeated, or invented to meet a length target.
Explicitly distinguish the study objective, hypothesis, and endpoints when they describe different constructs.
When the approved source does not define an instrument, scoring rule, denominator, missing-data method, date, or version, do not invent one or expose an internal source-gap note.
Do not use an evidence reference unless the returned prose or list actually contains the material fact it supports.

Every paragraph object and every list object must include at least one evidence_refs or boilerplate_refs value allowed by its section contract. If prose only introduces an already-cited list, omit that paragraph instead of returning empty reference arrays.

paragraphs.text: Your TECNIS PureSee or TECNIS Odyssey lens model must already have been selected for both eyes during routine clinical care before you enroll. The study will confirm that selection and place you in the matching lens group. At one operative visit for each eye, you will undergo cataract surgery and receive the planned lens model. The interval between the two surgeries will follow routine clinical care; the study does not specify a fixed interval.

After surgery, the study activities are measurements and monitoring rather than selection of your treatment. The vision tests use both eyes together. The study also includes the Assessment of IntraOcular Lens Implant Symptoms (AIOLIS) questionnaire, monitoring for adverse events and device deficiencies, and an exit form. All Month 1, Month 3, and Month 6 time points are measured from surgery on your second eye.

Information about adverse events and device deficiencies will be collected from the time you give consent through your final study contact. Although these are reviewed at the scheduled postoperative visits, you may report them at other times.

items: You must be 50 years of age or older and undergoing surgery for age-related cataracts in both eyes.
You must have planned bilateral implantation of either TECNIS PureSee or TECNIS Odyssey, with the lens model selected during routine clinical care before enrollment.
You must be willing and able to attend the scheduled study assessments.
You must not have participated in another study during the 60 days before screening.
You cannot take part if your surgeon determines that you have moderate-to-severe eye disease that increases the risk of complicated cataract surgery or prevents reliable visual-acuity testing.

You cannot take part if you have pseudoexfoliation syndrome with clinically significant zonular weakness, zonular dehiscence, a previous eye injury affecting vision, or previous corneal refractive surgery.
You cannot take part if different lens models are planned for your two eyes.

Screening, before surgery: You will give informed consent. The study team will collect demographic information and your medical history and will confirm your routine-care lens selection and corresponding study group.
Operative visits, one for each eye: You will undergo cataract surgery and implantation of the planned lens model.

Month 1, one month after second-eye surgery: You will have binocular uncorrected photopic distance visual-acuity testing, binocular corrected photopic distance visual-acuity testing, and binocular uncorrected photopic intermediate visual-acuity testing at 66 cm. The study team will monitor for adverse events and device deficiencies.

Month 3, three months after second-eye surgery: You will have binocular uncorrected and corrected photopic distance visual-acuity testing; binocular uncorrected photopic intermediate visual-acuity testing at 66 cm; and binocular uncorrected and distance-corrected photopic near visual-acuity testing at 40 cm. You will complete the AIOLIS questionnaire, and the study team will monitor for adverse events and device deficiencies.

Month 6 exit visit, six months after second-eye surgery: You will have binocular uncorrected and corrected photopic distance visual-acuity testing; binocular uncorrected and distance-corrected photopic intermediate visual-acuity testing at 66 cm; and binocular uncorrected and distance-corrected photopic near visual-acuity testing at 40 cm. You will also have a distance-corrected defocus-curve test, complete the AIOLIS questionnaire, be monitored for adverse events and device deficiencies, and complete the exit form.
